items: Browser resource health, CDP pid recovery and the node's browser pid-file repair check the browser with `kill -0` and "only listener on the slot's CDP port" (`lsof`) instead of `capture-helper resolve`. macOS keys ScreenCaptureKit clients by executable path, so each `resolve` exit stopped every capture-helper recording on that machine (SCStreamErrorDomain -3805); on macpro this killed Android mirror recordings within seconds. A browser with no CDP port is checked for liveness only

A run created with an explicit slot that is still releasing from its previous run waits up to 5 minutes for the release to land, counted as find-slot queue time, instead of failing at once as "busy (releasing)". Cancelling, pausing or replaying the run during the wait, or any time before its slot claim is written, stops it without claiming the slot. A claim whose write was already in flight when a cancel or pause landed is undone, fenced on the epoch it wrote: an ownership claim resets the slot, and a reservation (takeover or fresh reuse) drops itself and restores the fields it overwrote while the row still shows them beside the same owner, keeping any newer owner write, so it never strands the slot under the cancelled run. When the release outlasts the wait, or the slot has any other holder (including a rival run that claimed it as the release landed), the run fails with a message naming it: "release in progress since <time>", the live run's id and status, a handoff reservation, or an occupancy hold with its reason, since when and which run left it, and `farmslot slot release <slot>`. A slot left held after a run's teardown was skipped no longer fails as "mid-release or claimed by another live run"

Workers on a remote node reach the gateway that dispatched them. Worker launches, terminal and native, and every other shell Farmslot runs on that machine now export `GW_URL` set to the URL the node itself dials (reported in `node.connect`). Before, `farmslot` run from a slot fell back to that machine's operator profile in `~/.farmslot/gateways.json`, which on macpro and mini pointed at a `127.0.0.1:17801` tunnel that only exists on the operator's machine. A pool `env.GW_URL` still wins, and gateway-local slots are unchanged. No credential is added: worker shells still get no control-plane token, and the CLI authenticates with that node's stored profile for the same URL. The node's URL must be `ws`/`wss` with no embedded user or password, or it is ignored

`slot check` runs `node --version` and the slot's runner binaries (`claude`, plus `codex` when the pool sets `codex_path` or a project flow defaults to it) with `--version` in the slot repo, with the env a worker launch gets. A repo whose `.tool-versions` pins a Node version the host has not installed now fails `runner.node` with asdf's message, the pinned version and the fix (`asdf install` in the repo); it used to pass every check while the runner could not start. The probes run in parallel and stream each result, with a heartbeat while one is pending

`task.progress` with a `runId` whose slot no longer holds a task (released after the run finished) reads the run's recorded task directory on the gateway, the copy its artifacts are served from, when it lies under the project's task root: the worker's checked checklist (the `.worker` mirror; without it only acceptance data), operations and acceptance data (ledger or manifest links). It used to fail with "No task file for slot". `ORCHESTRATOR_LOCALITY` replaces three local copies of the gateway-filesystem locality
